sections.html: Platystomatichthys sturio is one of the most bizarre predatory catfish of Amazonia. The upturned snout-tip is species-specific, but its degree differs between individuals and also depends somewhat on age. The maximum length is about 40 cm. Available size: 7-16 cm.
The species has a very wide distribution in Amazonia. The animals offered originate from Peru.

The species has extremely long barbels and prefers to swim against a strong current. Platystomatichthys sturio is very peaceful towards conspecifics and other fish that are too large to be prey. The species is not shy at all and tends not to panic and crash into anything.

The sense or reason for the upturned snout-tip is unknown. Perhaps it helps to localize prey, or it may work like the spoiler of a car and save energy when swimming against the current. Some speculate that it is an artefact of aquarium keeping, caused by swimming against the glass, but this is unlikely, since almost all, even very small, specimens show it.

Platystomatichthys means "fish that looks like a Platystoma" (another genus of fish). sturio means "sturgeon", referring to the similar body shape.
